english.title: Drive a motor vehicle which had been taken without the owner's consent
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), knowing that a conveyance, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..) had been taken without the consent of the owner or other lawful authority, drove the said conveyance
english.legislation: Contrary to section 12(1) of the Theft Act 1968.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Mandatory drug test required if 18 or over
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This is a summary offence only, but sections 40 and 41 of the Criminal Justice Act 1988 provide that it may be joined in an indictment and dealt with at Crown Court in certain circumstances.
(ii) See also offence wordings H430, H434, H435, H439 and H2088.
(iii) See also aggravated T.W.O.C.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY ONLY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Discretionary disqualification.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see legislation

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
